meta.parties: Ibrahim Saibo and Another v. The Oriental Bank Corporation

rules.statement: Where the price for the purchase of certain lands was paid by one A, but the names of the plaintiffs were fraudulently entered in the conveyances as purchasers and as having paid the consideration, for the purpose of concealing the true ownership from A's creditors; and where the purchases were intended to be for A's benefit, and to withdraw from his creditors the purchase money and certain other large sums of money which he disbursed on the improvement of the lands and in erecting buildings on them; and where there was a secret understanding between A and plaintiffs that the latter should formally convey the lands to the former after he should compound with his creditors, and that in the meantime A should possess the lands as his own from the date of the conveyances to plaintiffs and with their knowledge and assent; and where at the date of the conveyances A was and ever since has been in insolvent circumstances, and where plaintiffs were parties to his fraud on his creditors- Held, that the plaintiffs were not entitled to a declaration of title to these lands, nor to have them released from seizure under a writ sued out by defendants as creditors of A.
